title: I actually shipped my first game using AI! It's a JRPG-inspired deckbuilder and already made 30 sales. Here's what I've learned.
author: Westwaage
selftext:
Hey everyone! I've been working on my first-ever game, Sunward Sentinel, and recently released it into Early Access on itch.io.

It's a JRPG-inspired tactical deckbuilder made in Godot, featuring 7 classes, 88 cards, a connected world map, 33 combat encounters, and 6 boss fights. I never got into games like Slay the Spire because I prefer playing games with full party members so I just made one myself.

AI has been central to the entire development process. I've primarily used Codex for programming, implementation, debugging, and testing, alongside AI image generation for some character artwork, animations, and visual effects.

One of the biggest things I've learned is how much iteration matters. Getting AI to produce something that technically works is one challenge. Getting it to look polished, animate consistently, and integrate properly with everything else can take quite a few rounds of revisions.

A recent example: I recently implemented a giant rattlesnake boss where the head and tail are independently targetable, and the tail can be killed and resurrected. Getting the different parts to animate together as one creature has been an interesting challenge! It's actually still not perfect and I need to ship out a correction for some of the visuals with it.

I'm excited that I've finally reached the point of shipping something playable. I used to start making games without ever getting them to be shipped in the past. Having AI enable me has been fun! There's still plenty I want to improve, but it's rewarding to see the project come together.

If anyone wants to check it out, here's the [itch.io](http://itch.io) page:

[https://gradientware.itch.io/sunward-sentinel](https://gradientware.itch.io/sunward-sentinel)

It's currently available for Windows at a discounted Early Access price of $5.99, which also includes the eventual full release.

Feedback on the combat, visuals, or overall gameplay would be very welcome!
